standard.title: Spatial representation and scale
standard.description: how places can be spatially represented in geographical divisions from local to regional to state/territory, and how people and places are interconnected across those scales
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y1 (AC9HS1K03): Students located natural, managed and constructed features on local maps using direction and location terms.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain how places can be spatially represented from local to state/territory scale and how people and places are interconnected across those scales.

nodes.label: Geographical divisions and scales
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the geographical divisions from local to regional to state/territory and locate where they live within this hierarchy using maps and a globe.
nodes.minimum_width: Locate their home in relation to their nearest capital city and state/territory on a map.
nodes.typical_width: Identify where they live in Australia in relation to nearest capital city, region and state/territory on maps and a globe; use geographical tools to explore scale from local to national.
wider: Locate Australia's position relative to neighbouring regions and countries on a globe
Compare the size and population of different states and territories and discuss why they differ
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding the local-to-state/territory scale hierarchy is prerequisite to understanding interconnections across scales — you cannot explain a connection between scales you cannot name or locate.

response_modes.reason: Scale is a new concept at Year 2 — repeated practice with maps, globes and digital tools at different scales builds the spatial vocabulary needed for interconnection discussions.

success_criteria: Locates home in relation to nearest capital city and state/territory on a map
Names the state/territory they live in and at least one neighbouring state

nodes.label: Interconnections across scales
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how they and their community are connected to people and places at regional and state/territory scale, including through movement, shopping, communication and transport.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two ways they are connected to a place outside their local area (e.g. visiting relatives, where food comes from, holidays).
nodes.typical_width: Investigate places locally and at broader scale that they and their families visit for shopping, health, recreation, religious or ceremonial activities; identify links with places at regional and state/territory scale; describe how communication and transport technologies connect places.
wider: Map the connections their family has to places at regional and state/territory scale and discuss why those connections exist
Explore how First Nations Australians' songlines connect places across Country and compare with contemporary travel routes

response_modes.reason: Each student's family connections are different — class sharing creates genuine breadth of interconnection examples.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Family interconnection maps genuinely vary by cultural background, economic circumstance and geographic origin — the class data set is rich and authentic.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two connections to places outside their local area
Explains how at least one connection is maintained (transport, communication, visits)
